investigations.name: bm-e1-actomyosin-cortex
investigations.description:
First mechanistic extension beyond the paper (plan section 5). A coarse actomyosin cortex
(filaments, crosslinks, motors) is built as a LAMMPS patch and characterised (tension,
strain response, relaxation), then mapped to the effective Tyssue cortical-energy
parameters. This is explicitly a NEW extension, not a reproduction target; its fidelity
decision (reduced cortical model vs molecularly-resolved actin) is an open decision in the
plan. Care is taken not to double-count tension when the effective cortical term is replaced
by explicit actin.
investigations.title: Explicit actomyosin cortex mechanics
investigations.objective: Can a coarse explicit actomyosin filament/crosslink/motor model reproduce the cortical tension, strain response and relaxation that an effective Tyssue cortical-energy term represents?
investigations.claim: A coarse actomyosin cortex carries a cortical tension that rises with contractility, giving a tension that can be mapped onto the vertex model's cortical energy.

investigations.name: bm-e2-actin-adhesion-collagen
investigations.description:
The actin-adhesion-collagen force-transfer extension (plan section 5). Active cortical
contractility from E1 is coupled through reversible basal linkers (attachment sites,
occupancy, forces, work) to a collagen IV BM patch from R2. Readouts are traction, linker
occupancy, network deformation and the relative relaxation set by linker and crosslink
kinetics. A single-cell patch is validated with prescribed-displacement and imposed-traction
tests before any multicellular coupling, avoiding double-counting of BM mechanics.
investigations.title: Actin–adhesion–collagen force transfer
investigations.objective: How does active cortical contractility transfer force through reversible basal adhesions into the collagen IV basement membrane?
investigations.claim: An active cortex transmits force through reversible basal linkers to a collagen membrane patch; the transmitted traction scales with linker occupancy and cortical tension.

investigations.name: bm-e3-closed-3d-lumenoid
investigations.description:
The closed lumenoid extension (plan section 5, 3D lumenoid level). A closed curved
epithelium with lumen volume/pressure and a BM shell is the full morphogenesis target. The
reduced-order BM law (validated in R4-R5) is used first; resolved LAMMPS patches or a
curved-network BM are tested second. Curvature-dependent effects on lumen growth and cell
shape are the new predictions beyond the flat-substrate paper.
investigations.title: Closed 3D lumenoid morphogenesis
investigations.objective: How do lumen pressure/volume and a basement-membrane shell set cell shape and curvature- dependent growth in a closed 3D lumenoid?
investigations.claim: A closed lumenoid with a lumen pressure and a basal membrane surface runs the vertex model; attaching an explicit membrane and reading curvature-dependent shape is next.

investigations.name: bm-e4-feedback-predictions
investigations.description:
The novel-prediction extension (plan section 5, E4) and the end state of the campaign. Each
new feedback hypothesis (growth-driven turnover, spatial BM heterogeneity, contractility-
dependent confinement, partial adhesion, network failure) is tested against matched one-way
/ uncoupled / uniform-material controls so that any departure from the paper is attributable
to the mechanism rather than to added complexity. These are predictions, explicitly
distinguished from reproductions. This evidence pass records the P3 coupling scaffold: the
bidirectional epithelium<->BM loop runs on the reduced-order effective BM, the three coupling
controls behave correctly, and the BM subcycling converges -- the well-posed contract the
feedback predictions above will be read against.
investigations.title: LAMMPS–Tyssue coupled lumenoid
investigations.objective: When do growth-driven turnover, spatial BM heterogeneity, contractility-dependent confinement, partial adhesion and network failure change cell height and lumenoid growth beyond the original paper?
investigations.claim: The epithelium and its collagen basement membrane are coupled both ways: the growing basal surface stretches the membrane and the membrane's stress pushes back on the cells as a basal tension. On the reduced-order (effective) BM path the bidirectional loop runs end-to-end, the three coupling controls (two-way / one-way / uncoupled) behave exactly as the mechanism demands, and subcycling the BM relaxation converges.

investigations.name: bm-r1-published-tissue-baseline
investigations.description:
Direct reproduction of the paper's homogeneous tissue-mechanics result (Barrientos Fig 1). A
fixed-volume prism/surface-tension cell model is coupled to a viscoelastic BM; the relative
BM stiffness and the relaxation/doubling-time ratio are swept to recover the regime topology
(reconstructed basal area and cell height, reversibility, regime boundaries). This is the P1
homogeneous reference the spatial Tyssue studies (R4-R5) are later compared against; it uses
an effective constitutive BM, not the explicit collagen network.
investigations.title: Reduced-order tissue-mechanics baseline
investigations.objective: How do basement-membrane stiffness and relaxation, relative to the proliferation (doubling) time, control growth-dependent epithelial confinement?
investigations.claim: The homogeneous prism model recovers the paper's confinement regimes: a fixed-volume cell grows TALL under a stiff, slowly-relaxing basement membrane and SPREADS flat under a soft, fast-relaxing one, with cell height rising monotonically along both the BM stiffness and the BM relaxation axes of the Figure 1G map.

investigations.name: bm-r2-collagen-network-rheology
investigations.description:
The molecular-scale reproduction (Barrientos Fig 2D-E) and the frozen R2 stress-test that
gate P0. The faithful collagen IV network (released NC1/7S angles, density and turnover
controls established in bm-v1/bm-v4) is driven through staged loading with the crosslink
chemistry switched on at several turnover rates. Molecule residence time and the macroscopic
stress-relaxation time are measured independently so their proportionality (Fig 2E) is a
genuine prediction, not an identity. Engine-level mechanics and run-to-run variance are
benchmarked here.
investigations.title: Faithful collagen IV network rheology
investigations.objective: Is basement-membrane stress relaxation proportional to collagen IV molecular residence (turnover) time?
investigations.claim: The faithful collagen IV network runs under staged loading; the quantitative match to the paper's stress traces and relaxation-vs-turnover slope is still in progress.

investigations.name: bm-r3-network-expansion-supply
investigations.description:
Reproduces the supply/loss/dilution decomposition of Barrientos Fig 2B-C. Three matched
conditions share one initial state and forcing; the readouts are network area expansion,
collagen concentration and connectivity (largest connected component). The study establishes
which combination of remodeling and insertion sustains a growing network, a prerequisite for
the growth-rheology coupling used by R4 and the perturbations in R6.
investigations.title: Network expansion & collagen supply
investigations.objective: Why are both crosslink remodeling and collagen replacement (insertion) necessary for sustained basement-membrane growth?
investigations.claim: The three supply conditions run from a shared initial state; matching the paper's ordering in network area, concentration and connectivity is in progress.

investigations.name: bm-r4-coupled-2d-epithelium
investigations.description:
The first spatial model (plan section 3, 2D planar level). A Tyssue polygonal sheet carries
a BM traction/area law calibrated from the R2 network rheology; cell height is inferred
through an explicit volume/prism relation. A homogeneous reference case must reproduce R1;
heterogeneous growth, division and cortical-tension variation then test whether the
confinement phase diagram is robust to explicit topology. Effective constitutive BM and
explicit LAMMPS BM are interchangeable alternatives here, not additive forces.
investigations.title: Coupled 2D epithelial sheet
investigations.objective: Do the paper's confinement regimes survive explicit cell topology and heterogeneous growth in a spatial 2D epithelium?
investigations.claim: A 2D epithelial sheet with an explicit cell-height degree of freedom relaxes under the vertex model; wiring the membrane traction and comparing confinement to the homogeneous baseline is in progress.

investigations.name: bm-r5-explicit-3d-confinement
investigations.description:
The explicit 3D reproduction (plan section 3, 3D monolayer level). Real cell heights and
basal expansion emerge from apical/basal/lateral surface energies and volume constraints
rather than an inferred prism relation. The no-BM / elastic-BM / relaxing-BM controls
isolate the BM-relaxation contribution to cell height. Establishing the cell-height and area
response here gates P2 and is the substrate for the closed lumenoid (E3).
investigations.title: Explicit 3D cell confinement
investigations.objective: Do growing 3D epithelial cells become taller when the basement membrane relaxes slowly?
investigations.claim: A 3D monolayer with volume and surface energies runs and yields per-cell heights; the no-membrane, elastic-membrane and relaxing-membrane controls are the next step.

investigations.name: bm-r6-perlecan-growth-perturbations
investigations.description:
Closes the reproduction campaign by propagating the turnover-inference results (Fig 3-6)
into predicted shapes (Fig 7). Collagen lifetime distributions for control, perlecan
gain/loss and growth-rate perturbations drive the relaxation->shape chain with explicit
uncertainty propagation. The study must keep quantities that are INFERRED from the timer
observation model distinct from quantities INDEPENDENTLY PREDICTED by the mechanical model,
per the plan's validation distinction.
investigations.title: Perlecan & growth perturbations on cell shape
investigations.objective: Does the inferred chain (collagen lifetime -> BM relaxation -> cell shape) reproduce the paper's perlecan and growth-rate intervention ordering, keeping inferred and predicted quantities distinct?
investigations.claim: Carrying an inferred collagen lifetime through BM relaxation to cell shape reproduces the paper's intervention ordering: perlecan gain gives taller cells than control, and loss gives flatter ones, with the inferred relaxation time (turnover) kept distinct from the predicted cell height (mechanics).

investigations.name: bm-v1-stage1-modulus-remodelling
investigations.title: Elastic modulus & remodelling-time separation
investigations.objective: Can the clean-room collagen IV network separate an elastic modulus from a viscous remodelling time, as the paper's staged protocol does?
investigations.claim: A coarse-grained collagen IV network (two-bead rods, stochastic NC1/7S crosslinks, no excluded volume) run through the spec's stage-1 protocol — stretch, hold, then switch the chemistry on — yields a separable elastic modulus and remodelling (stress-relaxation) time on real LAMMPS.

investigations.name: bm-v2-stress-vs-strainrate
investigations.title: Growth rheology: stress vs strain rate
investigations.objective: What is σ(ε̇), and where does the network cross from viscous to elastic?
investigations.claim: Imposing an equibiaxial in-plane strain rate ε̇ on the growing collagen IV network and reading the steady-state stress σ(ε̇) gives the effective viscosity η = σ/ε̇ (viscous at slow rates) and the rate at which the response turns elastic — the σ(ε̇) relation a vertex model needs.

investigations.name: bm-v3-junction-bending-rigidity
investigations.title: Rigidity percolation (central-force control)
investigations.objective: Can more crosslink connectivity rigidify the v1 network, or is bending required?
investigations.claim: This study originally explained the soft modulus as a central-force rigidity-percolation effect (z ≤ 3 < 4). The released code is not a central-force network — it sets junction angles (NC1 at 180° with stiffness 4.0, 7S at 155° and 60°) — so that explanation does not describe the published model, which carries those angles and is still soft (≈0.03 Pa). What this connectivity sweep actually shows is that with angles off (our earlier transcription) and the corrected parameters, the network is sub-isostatic (z tops out at ≈2.0) and soft — a property of the angle-off transcription, not of the paper.

investigations.name: bm-v4-junction-bending
investigations.title: Native junction-bending modulus
investigations.objective: Does junction bending yield the measurable modulus the vertex model needs?
investigations.claim: Junction bending is a released feature (an NC1 angle of stiffness 4.0 at 180°, plus 7S angles), not a new ingredient; how it is applied decides whether it gives a usable modulus. Pinning as-formed restraints on after assembly is ill-conditioned — the sign flips and no reproducible value emerges. Creating real harmonic angles as the crosslinks form, so the network equilibrates with them active (matching the released bond/react templates), gives a positive, well-conditioned, reproducible modulus. The released model is not floppy once its angles are active; its modulus is finite and strongly density-dependent.

investigations.name: bm-v5-porosity-bundling
investigations.title: Network porosity & strand bundling
investigations.objective: Does the v1 network reproduce the measured pore-size and bundling of a real BM?
investigations.claim: Of the two geometric readouts the model should reproduce, one is met and one is not. The simulated pore-size distribution reaches the measured corneal-EM band (72 ± 40 nm) at realistic density, while the protomers-per-strand distribution stays near 1, below the measured 5-7. The released NC1/7S topology has no lateral-association bond, so it cannot form multi-protomer strands — a limitation identified in advance.
